title: Direction Sense
intro: Direction questions track a person walking and turning, then ask the final direction or the straight-line distance from the start. Always draw the path on a North-up grid: North is up, East is right. Mark each leg with its length, apply left/right turns relative to the current facing, and the diagram answers everything. For distance between start and end, the legs usually form a right triangle — use Pythagoras.

items.name: Compass
items.formula: N up, S down, E right, W left

items.name: Shadow rule
items.formula: sunrise (E) → shadow West; sunset (W) → shadow East

topics.name: Basic Directions & Turns
topics.details: Track facing direction through each turn. A right turn rotates you clockwise (N→E→S→W); a left turn anticlockwise (N→W→S→E). Update the facing after every instruction, then state the final direction.

topics.name: Net Displacement (Pythagoras)
topics.details: Add up movement along the East-West axis and along the North-South axis separately (opposite directions cancel). The straight-line distance from start to finish is √(EW² + NS²).

solved.problem: Walk 3 km East, then 4 km North. Distance from start?
Walk 6 km North, then 8 km East. Distance from start?
Walk 5 km East, then 5 km West. Distance from start?
Walk 4 km East, 3 km North, 4 km West. Distance from start?
solved.solution: EW nets to 0, NS = 3 → 3 km North.

topics.name: Shadows & Time
topics.details: In the morning the sun is in the East, so shadows fall to the West; in the evening the sun is in the West, so shadows fall East. The shadow always points opposite the sun.

solved.problem: At sunrise, a pole's shadow falls towards?
solved.solution: Sun in East → shadow to the West.

solved.problem: At sunset, a tree's shadow falls towards?
solved.solution: Sun in West → shadow to the East.

solved.problem: A man faces his shadow in the morning. Which way does he face?
solved.solution: Morning shadow is West → he faces West.

solved.problem: In the morning, your shadow is to your left. Which way do you face?
solved.solution: Shadow West is on your left → you face North.

topics.name: Coded Directions
topics.details: Symbols redefine directions ('North means East, East means South…') — effectively a rotation of the compass. Replace every stated direction with its coded meaning, redraw the path, then answer.

solved.problem: If North = East, East = South, South = West, West = North. A man walks 'North'. Actual direction?
solved.solution: He moves East (the coded meaning of North).

shortcuts: Always draw on a North-up grid (N up, E right).
Net distance = √(net EW² + net NS²); opposite legs cancel.
Shadow is opposite the sun: morning → West, evening → East.
Coded directions just rotate the compass — substitute everywhere.
mistakes: Adding all leg lengths instead of netting opposite directions.
Getting shadow direction backwards (it is opposite the sun).
Applying a direction code to only part of the problem.
pyq: SSC asks a turns item and a Pythagoras-distance item nearly every Tier; coded directions and shadows appear in Tier 2. The North-up sketch solves all of them.
summary: Draw every path on a North-up grid, update facing through each turn (right = clockwise), and find start-to-end distance with √(net EW² + net NS²). Shadows fall opposite the sun, and coded directions are just a rotated compass applied consistently.
